label: dense; strongest when outputting n (and a/1/j/w/k/u/0/v/f)
explanation: Dense feature: active on ~52% of all steps and on nearly every sequence, at similar rates in the original and copy phases (lower at t=0,1). The only clear structure is in the copy phase, keyed on the token being output. Outputting n fires 99.9% of the time and gives the largest activations (top examples are n outputs, often inside runs of n). Outputting a, 1, j, w, k, u, 0, v or f also fires more often (rates 0.7-0.94). A lookahead to an upcoming n output (next_out == n) raises the activation too. The out-token-set predicate scores precision 0.85 but recall only 0.27 and mass recall 0.37 on dev. The rest of the mass is spread broadly over original-phase steps with no capturable predicate. The trivial predicate t>=2 gets F1 0.68 and adds no insight.
